key_insight: The intact brain–skull interface exhibits cohesive failure within the subarachnoid space, rather than behaving as a rigid connection or frictionless sliding contact.
engineering_relevance: An experimentally calibrated cohesive zone model offers more realistic brain–skull boundary conditions for computational head models.
method: Tested native brain–skull specimens from 19 sheep cadaver heads in tension, compression and shear.
Used histology to verify interface integrity and MRI to construct sample-specific finite element models.
Sequentially calibrated Ogden brain tissue and cohesive interface parameters using inverse finite element analysis.
evidence_signal: Interface properties showed no significant strain-rate or loading-mode dependence, with peak normal traction of 2.35 ± 0.81 kPa, peak tangential traction of 4.14 ± 0.97 kPa and fracture energy of 0.35 ± 0.14 N/m.
watch_item: Transfer to human head models and impact-rate loading requires validation beyond sheep cadaver specimens and the tested strain rates.
paper_title: Mechanical behaviour of the intact brain-skull interface under tension, compression and shear
